newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians, Tajik rebels clash on Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Russians, Tajik rebels clash on Afghan border.

text.p: Russian troops and Tajik rebels clashed on the border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan on Sunday but news agencies said soldiers had stopped the rebels, who were trying to cross into the former Soviet republic.
There were no reports of casualties on Sunday among the Russian troops guarding the border, on the southern edge of the former Soviet Union.
Earlier reports said one Russian soldier was killed after a group of Tajik opposition guerrillas broke through from Afghanistan on Saturday.

Itar-Tass news agency, quoting Russian military sources, said the soldiers had fought off attempts by 200 rebels and a smaller number of Afghan fighters to cross the frontier. But the situation remained "very complex".
Tass said on Saturday the guards had been put on alert because of tension in Afghanistan.
But the latest incidents did not appear to be linked with fighting in Afghanistan, where the Taleban movement has seized the capital Kabul and introduced strict Islamic law.
The Tajik rebels are loyal to Islamic opposition leaders driven into exile in Afghanistan and Iran after losing a clan-based civil war which broke out soon after independence from the Soviet Union.
A border guards' spokesman said on Saturday there had been about 30 attempts to break through since the start of the year, 20 of which resulted in armed clashes.
